capabilities.claim: Researches the codebase and drafts a 'Blueprint' (spec with plan and tests); nothing is built until approved. Help center defines a three-phase spec framework (product, UX, technical); specs can be user-written or agent-drafted.
capabilities.notes: Docs mostly frame specs as user-authored ('agents write exactly what you describe'); agent drafting mentioned in 'Your First Initiative'. Blueprints are edited in place, no version history documented. No public demo of spec generation found.

capabilities.claim: Orchestrator plans and hands tasks to worker agents; work hierarchy initiative > feature > executable (one task, one agent, one PR) with dependency ordering and statuses.
capabilities.notes: Docs describe hierarchy and statuses; public GitHub shows ~5,700 PRs from obvious-autobuild[bot] across many repos, consistent with orchestrated multi-PR work. Internal orchestrator design not documented in detail; Build Blog 'Orchestration Layer' is a review-SLA dashboard marked 'In Development'.

capabilities.claim: Each worker agent runs in its own cloud sandbox; independent executables run concurrently; sandbox is a pre-built checkout of the repo, changes made 'without changing your main branch'.
capabilities.notes: Public PR (chromaui/chromatic-cli#1521) shows a named sandbox snapshot ID and per-repo snapshot, partially demonstrating per-repo sandboxes. Isolation technology (VM/container/network policy) not disclosed. Per-agent isolation is a vendor claim.

capabilities.claim: Automated code review agent with generic rubric customizable via .obvious/review/ (overlay rules, scoring 0-100 mapped to Blocker/High/Medium/internal/silent); path-based routing (none/single/specialized); reading guide per PR; human merge can be required.
capabilities.notes: Independence of reviewer from author agent (separate model/context) is not described. In observed Storybook PRs, review came largely from the customer's own bots (Greptile, storybook-contribution-review) and human maintainers, not visibly from Obvious's reviewer.

capabilities.claim: QA runs same criteria every time, attaches screenshots, videos, test results, API responses; failed checks auto-fixed and retested. Build Blog: headless browser against preview deploy, 16-frame 'sprites', semantic diffs attached as PR comments.
capabilities.notes: Public onboarding PR #1521 lists install/build/lint/typecheck results and test counts (1534 passed) and explicitly states what was not run. Visual evidence pipeline (Closed-Loop Agents) is marked 'In Development' on vendor blog; no public screenshot/video evidence observed in sampled PRs.

capabilities.claim: Repo contract in .obvious/: config.yml (base branch, merge method, review routing, CI generated-file commands, preview envs, QA paths), obvious.md, skills, runbooks. Workspace settings requireHumanMerge / requireHumanCreatePR. Repo config cannot weaken platform safety rules or branch protection. Draft-early PRs always on.
capabilities.notes: Public onboarding PRs by obvious-autobuild[bot] add .obvious/config.yml, obvious.md, codebase-map.md, skills/ to real repos. Several config keys (notifications, release, owners, runbooks, humanReview.requestPolicy) are reserved/not consumed.

capabilities.claim: Repo skills as .obvious/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (frontmatter name/description/triggers), optional SKILL_CORE.md injected every turn; discovered from default branch only, cached 15 min; knowledge sources include codebase, past PRs, docs, incidents, ADRs; AGENTS.md honored; workspace/project/user memory.
capabilities.notes: Skill format is documented in detail; public PR #1521 shows a generated skills/local-dev/SKILL.md. No skill versioning or precedence rules documented. Knowledge-source ingestion (incidents, ADRs) is marketing-level only.

capabilities.claim: Learns from chats and ratings; nightly memory consolidation (dedupe, compress, promote to workspace); daily scan of recurring review issues proposes up to 3 fixes with supporting reviews; 3 identical notes -> drafted rule; memory updates automatic, rule/skill/loop changes require human approval (approve/edit/discard); 'Un-apply' removes a rule; scope per person/project/global; agent-to-agent messages never become memory.
capabilities.notes: Marketing page only; no help-center article found on rule approval/versioning. No version history documented for rules; rollback = 'Un-apply' that rebuilds instructions. Memory changes are NOT human-gated. Whether approved changes are written back to repo skills via PR is not stated. Dashboard metrics on the page are illustrative.

capabilities.claim: Spend tracked per task, project, workspace; build drawer shows duration and cost 'when one is recorded'; Spend Controls with monthly org budget, daily throttles, per-user/per-project allocations; dashboard shows cost/PR, autonomy %, leaderboard of credits per builder; review SLA dashboard (in development).
capabilities.notes: Human-attention metrics (autonomy %, review latency) shown only as illustrative dashboards; orchestration dashboard 'In Development'. Credits help page appears partly out of date (mentions Team plans, Fast/Deep modes).

capabilities.claim: Blueprint approval before build; custom loops can add human approval points; build drawer surfaces decisions awaiting input; requireHumanMerge / requireHumanCreatePR; protected credentials require inbox approval; self-improvement rule changes require approval; generic agent plans support Stop-before/after and Allow/Review/Block permission gates.
capabilities.notes: Public PRs show humans (repo maintainers) approving and merging bot PRs, e.g. storybook#37512 merged by a maintainer. Formal spec approval gate is in marketing copy but not described in spec help article. Applicability of generic agent plan gates to Autobuild unconfirmed.

capabilities.claim: Fusion routes each step to a model class and reasoning depth; pin a model per chat/agent/routine or workspace default; listed models: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash; Max mode 2-3x credits; provider failover; Enterprise bring-your-own/custom models and fine-tuning.
capabilities.notes: Gemini not listed. BYO model setup details not documented. Which models AutoBuild coding agents use by default is not disclosed.

capabilities.claim: Intake from Slack, tickets, triggers, schedules; Autobuild home with builds list and build drawer; Factory Cockpit and Inbox; PRs page; desktop and mobile apps; GitHub App (plus GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps listed); integrations with Linear, Jira, Notion, Atlassian, CI and observability tools; 'babysit' stalled PRs.
capabilities.notes: GitHub-side DX observable in public PRs (draft-early PRs, follow-up commits addressing reviewer comments, links back to Obvious project/thread/artifact). In-app UI not independently reviewed; no public video demo located.

capabilities.claim: Security onboarding scan before agent access; per-repo sandboxes; GitHub App scoped to selected repos; platform safety rules and permission gates not overridable by repo config; secrets scoped (user/team/workspace/project), protected secrets need per-use approval (15 min once / 30 min session); secrets stored separately from prompts; ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR/CCPA, HIPAA-ready; AES-256/TLS 1.3; SSO/SAML/OIDC, SCIM, RBAC, MFA, immutable audit logs, IP allowlists.
capabilities.notes: Certifications are vendor-asserted; no public trust center / report found. Sandbox isolation tech, network egress controls, GitHub App permission scopes, and whether sandboxed code can read raw secret values are not documented.

capabilities.claim: Preview environments in config.yml (URL templates, readiness polling, timeouts); agents own PRs through merge (CI fixes, review rounds); scheduled/triggered work; continues while laptop closed; Enterprise on-premise deployment option (pricing page).
capabilities.notes: Production deployment/release automation is not documented (release/notifications keys reserved, unused). Continuous maintenance inferred from public PR stream: ongoing flaky-test, CI, and migration PRs in storybookjs/storybook and other repos. On-prem listed on pricing page but not on enterprise page (inconsistent).

own_observation_github.caveats: Public repos only; merger identity not checked at scale; many repos are small/personal; does not measure quality.
